claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I need to understand your situation better. Let me begin with a few key questions:

**What is the full name of the child (or children) you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about my son Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd be happy to help you determine if you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some details about Alex's situation. Let me start with the basics:

**How old is Alex, and what is his date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old. His birthday is in March - he turned 8 earlier this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now, to continue the assessment:

**Does Alex live with you, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK? Also, do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that you're based in Manchester. That's useful context.

To ensure I have the complete picture, I need to check one more important detail:

**What is your nationality or immigration status? For example, are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Before I can make a final assessment, I need to check a few more important details about Alex's circumstances:

**Is Alex in full-time education or training, or does he have any other special circumstances I should know about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's just in primary school - nothing special really. He's a typical 8-year-old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to make sure I have everything I need, let me ask a couple more clarifying questions:

**Has Alex ever been looked after by a local authority, or is he currently in care or in hospital on a long-term basis?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he was in local authority care for a little while earlier this year, but that's finished now. He's been back home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important detail. I need to understand this situation better:

**When exactly was Alex in local authority care earlier this year? Specifically, when did he leave care and return home to live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was a couple of months that he was in care. He came back home to me after that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to get a bit more clarity on the timing to assess this properly:

**Can you tell me the approximate months when Alex was in care and when he returned home? For example, was it January to March, or April to June, etc.?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was around 7 weeks actually, now that I think about it more carefully. It ended a few weeks ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just to be precise about the timeline:

**Approximately when did those 7 weeks end? Can you tell me which month that was - for instance, was it in September, August, or another month?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was recent - just wrapped up a few weeks back, so that would have been late October, early November time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's very helpful.

I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me review the rules to make sure I give you an accurate answer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the Child Benefit eligibility rules, I can now provide you with my assessment:

**You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

1. **Basic eligibility criteria met:** You are a British citizen living in the UK (Manchester), and Alex is under 16 and lives with you at home. These are the fundamental requirements.

2. **Regarding the period in care:** Alex was in local authority care for approximately 7 weeks, which ended in late October/early November. According to the rules, Child Benefit can be affected if a child is in care for **more than 8 weeks**. Since Alex was only in care for 7 weeks (less than 8 weeks), this period does not disqualify you from receiving Child Benefit.

3. **Current situation:** Alex is now back home living with you, so you meet the requirement of being responsible for a child under 16 who lives with you.

You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already done so, you can apply through HMRC.
